post.contentHtml:
At a Glance: Kuriyama Holdings (3355, Tokyo Stock Exchange)

Kuriyama Holdings is a mid-sized Japanese company that makes industrial rubber and resin hoses, construction materials for roads and bridges, and flooring and artificial turf for sports facilities. It also runs a hose business in North America. This article centers on one question: "Why is a company that has already hit three-quarters of its annual target in the first half still trading at around 9x earnings?"

1. What the Numbers Say: Roughly 75% Progress

The company set its ordinary profit target for the fiscal year ending December 2026 at 5.4 billion yen (ordinary profit is close to pre-tax profit, combining operating and financial income and expenses). That is an increase of about 11.9% from the previous year. Based on the interim results announced in August 2026, progress toward this target was about 74.9%. Since the usual benchmark at the half-year mark is around 50%, this is a fairly fast pace.

ItemDetails
H1 2026 revenue (aggregated)Approx. 51.3 billion yen
H1 operating profit (aggregated)Approx. 3.6 billion yen
H1 net profit (aggregated)Approx. 2.7 billion yen
Company ordinary profit forecast (full year)5.4 billion yen
Market consensus (full year)Approx. 6.2 billion yen

The fact that the market consensus is higher than the company's own target may suggest that investors view the company's guidance (the earnings outlook the company itself provides) as conservative. However, this is only an interpretation, not a confirmed fact. Many Japanese companies see costs concentrated in the second half or have seasonal factors, so first-half progress alone cannot determine full-year results.

2. Share Price and Valuation

The most recent confirmed quote (closing price on October 23) was 1,728 yen, with a P/E ratio (share price ÷ earnings per share, a measure of price relative to profit) of about 9.0x, a P/B ratio (share price ÷ net assets per share) of about 0.65x, and a market capitalization of about 38.5 billion yen. According to the data provided, the share price in early November was around 1,640 yen, and the one-year price change was -0.06%, effectively flat. The 52-week range is 1,444 yen to 2,021 yen (the high was set in April 2026).

  • P/B below 1x: This means the market capitalization is smaller than the company's net assets. It is a zone drawing attention as the Tokyo Stock Exchange has been pushing companies with a P/B below 1x to improve.
  • Dividend: The expected dividend yield is confirmed at around 3.5%.
  • Analysts: The average target price is about 2,400 yen, but very few analysts cover the stock, so it should be treated as a reference only.

3. Why Does It Look Cheap? Factors to Consider

  • Low liquidity: The median annual daily trading value is small, at about 42 million yen, making it hard for institutional money to come in. This is presumed to be a typical cause of a small-cap discount.
  • Complex business mix: With businesses spread across hoses, construction materials, sports flooring and hotels, it lacks a growth story that can be explained in one line.
  • Shareholder structure: The largest shareholder is an individual connected to the Kuriyama family (about 6.7%), followed by NOK (about 4.9%) and the employee shareholding association (about 4.0%). There has been no change in the past few weeks. Japan's national pension fund does not hold the stock.
  • Price action: The stock has corrected since its April high, and as of late October its technical signal was shown as "continued decline."

4. Checkpoints Right Now

The company's Q3 2026 earnings announcement was scheduled for November 12. At the time of my search, I could not confirm the specific figures or whether guidance was revised. Please check the filings directly for the items below.

  • Whether cumulative Q3 ordinary profit has already exceeded the company target of 5.4 billion yen, and if so, whether an upward revision was issued
  • Margin changes in the North American hose business and the domestic construction materials segment
  • How the dividend policy (an aggregated H1 dividend of about 61 yen) is maintained on a full-year basis
  • Any mention of capital policy related to P/B improvement (share buybacks, higher dividends)

Summary

Kuriyama Holdings is a stock whose share price has moved sideways for a year despite fast earnings progress. Low liquidity and business complexity may be causes of the discount, and the key question is whether the Q3 filing becomes a catalyst for a re-rating. Conversely, if second-half earnings slow or trading volume keeps drying up, the undervaluation could persist for a long time.

This article is not investment advice, and investors are responsible for their own investment decisions.
